prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right attorney depends on the facts of your crash, how serious your injuries are, whether your case will likely settle or go to trial, and what style of lawyer you prefer. I can’t look up current local rankings, but I can help you find the best lawyer for your situation and evaluate candidates.

Quick guidance
- If your injuries are minor and you only need help with an insurance claim, a firm that handles lots of car-accident claims and negotiates well with insurers may be fine.
- If you have serious injuries, permanent impairment, complex liability, or the insurance company is refusing to pay, look for a trial lawyer with a strong record of verdicts and large settlements in similar cases.
- Act quickly: Texas’s statute of limitations for most personal injury claims is 2 years from the date of the crash.

Where to search for Houston attorneys
- Texas State Bar lawyer referral service / Houston Bar Association referral
- Super Lawyers (Texas/Houston listings)
- Martindale-Hubbell (ratings and peer reviews)
- Avvo / Google / Yelp (client reviews; use cautiously)
- Local recommendations from friends/family or other lawyers (if you have one in a different specialty)

What to look for (must-haves)
- Substantial experience with car-accident and personal-injury cases in Houston and Texas courts
- Trial experience (if your case may require it)
- Documented results (settlements/verdicts) in similar cases
- Clear contingency-fee agreement and explanation of costs/expenses
- Good communication: who handles your calls and updates
- Willingness to advance case costs (medical record fees, expert fees) if needed
- No disciplinary history with the Texas Bar

Red flags
- Guarantees of results
- No written fee agreement or unwillingness to put terms in writing
- Poor client communication or evasive answers about their experience
- Unwillingness to take cases to trial if necessary

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How long have you been handling car-accident personal injury cases?
- What percentage of your practice is car wreck/personal injury?
- Have you handled cases like mine? Can you share outcomes (settlement/verdict amounts)?
- Will you handle my case personally or will associates/adjusters do most of the work?
- Do you have trial experience? How many jury trials have you tried?
- How do you charge (contingency percentage, court costs, medical lien handling)?
- Who pays case expenses up front and how are they repaid?
- What is your expected timeline and likely case value range?
- How will we communicate and how often?

Documents to gather before meeting lawyers
- Police report
- Photos of the crash scene and vehicles
- Medical records, bills, and records of treatment
- Pay stubs/loss-of-income documentation
- Insurance information (your policy and the other driver’s)
- Witness names and contact info
- Any correspondence from insurers

Typical contingency-fee info
- Many personal injury attorneys work on contingency (they are paid a percentage of the recovery). Common ranges in Texas are about 33% for pre-suit settlements, sometimes higher if a suit is filed or if the case goes to trial. Always get the exact percentage and expense rules in writing.

If you want, I can:
- Help you draft a short message/email to send to lawyers when requesting a consultation.
- Create a one-page checklist to take to consultations.
- Narrow down a shortlist if you give me more details about your crash (severity, who’s at fault, any disputes, where in Houston it happened, whether insurers have made offers).

Which would you like to do next?
